audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart hands Rumble four of seven stages and Zaahen none, on a matchup Rumble wins 45.91% of 562 games. The packet flags this contradiction directly. The prose matches the bad chart: 'his stage is over', 'he never gets his duel', 'late you dictate the sidelane'.
audit.why: A chart that never lets the enemy win a single stage cannot describe a lane the owner loses. Zaahen's kit says where the stages belong: Grim Deliverance is a 110-second all-in that heals him for a portion of the damage it deals, and Cultivation of War banks bonus Attack Damage off every attack and ability he lands on a champion and lets him revive at full stacks. Both are late-arriving, both beat Rumble's short-trade pattern.
audit.corrected: Give Zaahen Level 6 and Two-plus items, downgrade First item to Skill, and keep Rumble's genuine window at levels 2-3. That leaves 2 Rumble / 2 Zaahen / 3 Skill, which is honest for a 45.91% lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike is described in terms of Rumble only ('the AP spike', 'the Q heat zone') and not one Zaahen ability is named anywhere in the matchup — not in spikes, wants, whys, or prose.
audit.why: Zaahen's spikes are nameable and countable: The Darkin Glaive (10/9/8/7/6, auto reset, heals, recast knocks up), Dreaded Return (14s at rank 1, 850-range pull), Aureate Rush (10s at rank 1 dash), Grim Deliverance (110s at rank 1, damage plus heal). Without those the spike list is generic filler.
audit.corrected: Attach the real names and rank-1 cooldowns to each spike so the player knows what is arriving and when.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup repeatedly calls Zaahen's mobility weak — 'his weak gap-close cannot answer the zone', 'against his lack of gap-close'. He has two ways in. Aureate Rush is a dash on 10/9.5/9/8.5/8, and Dreaded Return stabs at 850 range and PULLS the target toward him. 850 is exactly Electro-Harpoon's range, so the spacing Rumble thinks is safe is the spacing Zaahen wants. Also missing: The Darkin Glaive is an auto-attack reset with a knock-up recast, and both it and Grim Deliverance heal him.
audit.why: Riot's text for Dreaded Return: 'Zaahen stabs in a direction, damaging enemies hit, then pulls them toward him,' range 850. Rumble's Electro-Harpoon is also 850. Telling a Rumble that his opponent cannot close is the single most dangerous error possible in a lane built on spacing. The Darkin Glaive's autoReset flag plus 'slashes twice on his next attack' makes the wind-up the tell, and the heal on Q and R is what Grievous Wounds exists for.
audit.corrected: Delete the weak-gap-close claim, state Dreaded Return's 850-range pull against Rumble's own 850 harpoon, give Aureate Rush its 10s rank-1 dash, flag the Darkin Glaive auto reset as the step-back cue, and put anti-heal on the item line.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Late you dictate the sidelane... let his sustain bleed out chasing a target he can never reach' inverts the actual win condition on a lane Rumble loses.
audit.why: Cultivation of War grants stacking Attack Damage per stack gained from attacks and abilities on champions, and at full Determination he gains increased Attack Damage and can revive. A long kite-brawl is the fight that feeds it. Rumble's win condition is teamfight Equalizer and refusing the side lane, not out-lasting him.
audit.corrected: Flip the late-game to Equalizer-in-teamfights and explicit refusal of the extended sidelane duel.

edits.after: At 6 the lane turns. Grim Deliverance is a 110-second all-in that heals him for a share of the damage it deals, so it beats a mistimed wall outright. edits.after: Late you do not dictate the sidelane. Cultivation of War banks bonus AD off every attack he lands on you, and at full Determination he revives, so a long brawl ends his way even when you were winning it. Kite with harpoon, spend Equalizer on where the teamfight happens, and never take the flame duel at low heat.
